newsitem.title: USA: Sears chairman Martinez's bonus rose in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Sears chairman Martinez's bonus rose in 1996.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co chairman and chief executive Arthur Martinez saw his bonus payment rise to $1.9 million in 1996 from $1 million in 1995, according to the retailer's proxy statement for its annual meeting.
His salary for the year was $1.1 million, compared to $1.0 million in 1995, the proxy said.
The rise in the bonus was due to a shift that links more of executive compensation to the retailer's performance, as well as improved performance by the company in 1996, Sears said.

Martinez also received a $3 million payout in March 1996 from a long-term incentive payment plan for incentive pay accrued from 1993 to 1995, the proxy said. Additionally, Martinez received stock options worth $555,468 in present value at the date they were granted, the proxy said.
Sears will hold its annual meeting May 8 in Chicago.
Among matters to be voted on is a shareholder proposal that the company's board of directors be elected annually, rather than in the current staggered three-year terms.
